quote.text: What we obtain too cheap, we esteem too lightly: it is dearness only that gives every thing its value.
quote.author: Thomas Paine, The American Crisis (1776)

stories.kicker: Iran & the Gulf · The tanker war turns into a shooting war
stories.headline: Five tankers down, and Brent over a hundred
stories.dek: What last week was an Iranian “exclusion zone” became, over five days, a two-way exchange of fire at sea — the US sinking Iranian crude carriers, Iran firing on a base in Jordan, and the oil price breaking the round number the strait always threatens.

stories.kicker: Buy It Once · The weekender bag
stories.headline: The cabin bag, from the hide up
stories.dek: One holdall for a weekend or a flight to Tokyo, bought once. The word “leather” hides a four-tier con, the humid answer is not the pretty one, and the last two thousand dollars buys a name, not a bag.

stories.kicker: The Big Picture · One barrel, three tightenings
stories.headline: The oil shock the central banks can’t ignore
stories.dek: A single force is pricing everything this week: the tanker war put Brent through $100, headline inflation is reaccelerating, and three-plus major central banks are tightening into the same barrel — a configuration that leaves the balanced portfolio with no cushion.

stories.kicker: Politics · The pay review comes to the House
stories.headline: A million-dollar raise, and a relief cheque, in one week
stories.dek: The 2026 salary review was in the ledger as a scheduled line. The delta is that it reached the floor of Parliament on Monday, and the country has been arguing about it ever since — days after a cost-of-living payout landed in the same accounts.

stories.headline: Samsung writes Europe a €3bn cheque
stories.dek: Mistral raised the largest equity round in European tech history — led by a Korean chipmaker, joined by a Dutch lithography giant and a sovereign state — to own compute rather than rent it. The premium is on sovereignty; the question is whether the revenue is real.

stories.kicker: Gear · Android XR arrives on the face
stories.headline: The glasses are ready. The cable isn’t.
stories.dek: XREAL made its Aura glasses official at IFA — the first proper Android XR device, with Gemini built in — and took ten thousand reservations. What it did not do is quote a firm price or a firm date, and the compute still lives on a cable.

stories.kicker: Objects · A Geneva seal on a steel case
stories.headline: The movement earns it. The metal doesn’t.
stories.dek: Chopard’s new L.U.C 1963 chronograph pairs a hand-wound, column-wheel flyback with a Poinçon de Genève — genuine haute horlogerie — in a steel case at nearly €37,000. It is the premium question in one watch.

stories.kicker: Venice · The Lido’s loudest fourteen minutes
stories.headline: A CIA thriller, and a Lion still in its cage
stories.dek: Martin McDonagh’s first film in four years drew the festival’s longest ovation. But the Golden Lion is not decided until Saturday — so the story this issue is the race, not the result.

stories.kicker: Screens · The age check is coming — but not this term
stories.headline: An age gate for the accounts
stories.dek: Singapore will make age assurance mandatory on the big platforms, restricting under-13s from accounts. For a Primary 6 pupil that is a direct hit — but it is 2027 law, and the best-evidenced lever this term is still bedtime.

stories.headline: The two-track jump from bedroom to booth
stories.dek: You can start tonight for the price of a good dinner. What hooks people is the first clean transition — two records locked, the bass swapped, and nobody hears the seam. Everything after that is the descent.

stories.kicker: The Long Game · The dose, and where more buys nothing
stories.headline: Two hours of lifting, and not a minute more
stories.dek: A 147,000-person Harvard analysis put the longevity sweet spot for strength training at 90 to 120 minutes a week — and found no extra benefit past it. For a busy mid-forties reader, the good news is the ceiling. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.kicker: What’s Worth Booking · The dated agenda
stories.headline: What to book this week — and to plan the flights for
The nasi lemak, paid in three
stories.dek: In Malaysia, “Beli Sekarang, Bayar Kemudian” stopped being about wanting things and became about affording them. The average instalment is about ninety ringgit — groceries, fuel, a phone bill — and a brand-new regulator is racing to defuse it before it blows.
